we study a variant of a multi-period martingale optimal transportation problem to derive robust price upper bounds on a financial option, and that we introduce a time homogeneity assumption on the forward-looking martingale transitions, which improves the quality of the price bounds by incorporating more market data.

(i) we introduce a new multi-period martingale transport problem with time-homogeneous transitions of the martinegale, (ii) we provide a dual formulation of the problem, (iii) we illustrate the approach in two numerical examples

the question of how to use historical market data to derive bounds on the prices of financial derivatives.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new approach to derive price bounds on a European call option by using martingale optimal transportation and time consistency.
we provide a novel approach to the martingale transport problem in a time-homogeneous setting and derive price bounds for a derivative.
the time-homogeneous martingale transport approach provides robust price bounds for financial derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the standard martingale optimal transportation, we do not need to assume the existence of a market-consistent martingale measure to obtain price bounds.
the time-homogeneous martingale transport problem can provide robust and accurate bounds on financial derivative prices, which can be used for calibration of the underlying market model.
the martingale transport problem can be used as a framework to derive robust price estimates for financial derivatives in multi-period settings.
